name: time_given_in_the_customer_s_own
use_case: Book an appointment by service, staff, language, location and time zone
branch: Time given in the customer's own zone: CU442 Oliver Hughes, who lives in London (profile Europe/London), wants a massage with Olivia Bennett at Midtown on Tuesday 3 November 'at 3 pm my time'. New York's clocks went back on 1 November, so 15:00 London is 10:00 New York (UTC-05:00).
tests: the desk converts 3:00 pm London time to 10:00 am Midtown local time (UTC-05:00) and confirms both zones
instruction:
You live in London (Europe/London time zone) and want to book a Massage Therapy appointment with Olivia Bennett at the Midtown studio in New York for Tuesday 3 November 2026 at 3:00 pm your London time. You know New York's clocks change in early November, so 3:00 pm London time corresponds to 10:00 am New York time (2026-11-03T10:00, UTC-05:00). When the desk clarifies and reads back the time as 10:00 am New York time / 3:00 pm London time, confirm the booking.

Your details:
- Name: Oliver Hughes
- Email: oliver.hughes@example.com
- Phone: +44 20 7946 0442
- Home time zone: Europe/London
- Service: Massage Therapy
- Staff: Olivia Bennett
- Studio: Midtown Studio (New York)
- Date: Tuesday 3 November 2026
- Requested time: 3:00 pm London time (10:00 am New York time / 2026-11-03T10:00)

persona.name: Oliver Hughes
persona.initial_message: Hello, I'd like to book a massage with Olivia Bennett at Midtown on Tuesday November 3rd at 3:00 pm my time (London). My email is oliver.hughes@example.com and phone is +44 20 7946 0442.
